exposure: Peak total bile acid levels (μmol/L): mild (10-19), low moderate (20-39), high moderate (40-99), and severe (>100)
outcome: Cesarean delivery for nonreassuring fetal heart tracing
cohort: 1202 singleton, nonanomalous gestations complicated by intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
finding: Increasing severity of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm labor, iatrogenic preterm birth, and meconium-stained amniotic fluid but not other adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: While the study investigated the association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy severity and various outcomes, including cesarean delivery, it did not find a significant association between disease severity and mode of delivery.
